carries.from: the round-9 pull request F3.1 (stored instants; branch handoff/r9-f3-stores-1), which lands the N-future-instant store boundary and the stored-instant rule drift.stored_instant at the F3 lane's loaders
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. With the rule attaching UTC to a naive stamp in boost._parse_until, the stub's default naive clock (HASTUB_TZ unset) made boost.restore raise TypeError comparing the aware stored end with the naive now, and tests/features.py and tests/finite_boundary.py both exited 1 on it at the branch's first cut; with the zone taken from dt_util.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE (None in the stub) both pass (ALL 3380 FEATURE CHECKS PASSED, ALL 46 FINITE BOUNDARY CHECKS PASSED), and under a configured zone the value loads aware (the features.py pin 'boost, the pump-duty arbiter and legionella read a naive stored stamp in Home Assistant's zone, aware'; mutant boost reading UTC turns it red).
carries.remeasure: Do not trust these results: they are at F3.1's head. At your merge base, run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/features.py` and read the section 'P1/P2 — a stored instant loads aware, or not at all'; then edit the zone argument of one loader to UTC and confirm the stub-clock suite fails as described.
carries.brief: Use `drift.stored_instant` for every stored instant F1.6 loads: a loader that can see Home Assistant passes `dt_util.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`, which reads a naive value in Home Assistant's zone and leaves it naive under the stub's naive clock; a pure loader with no clock takes the UTC default, which is `Cusum`'s pre-existing rule. The P1 barrier's Arm 4 refuses a naive instant held live, so it must drive an aware clock (set HASTUB_TZ or freeze an aware instant), or it refuses the stub's own naive stamps rather than a defect.

carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. Stored naive stamps loaded through the real arbiter, legionella and boost stores under a frozen clock at 12:00 local: at F3.2's merge base (the store reading every naive leaf as UTC) Stockholm pulled an honest stamp an hour old back to two hours old and dropped an honest boost with an hour left, and Los Angeles let a stamp six hours ahead through a lead of 0 and a boost end six hours ahead through a lead of two hours; at F3.2's head each honest stamp is kept and each one beyond its lead lands on now plus the lead, in both zones (the features.py check 'the store bounds a naive stored instant in its loader's zone'); deleting the naive_zone argument from any one of the three stores turns that check red again.

carries.brief: F1.6: a loader that reads a naive stored instant in Home Assistant's zone (`drift.stored_instant` with `dt_util.DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE`) constructs its `QuarantiningStore` with the same zone as `naive_zone`, or the store bounds that leaf as UTC and is off by the zone's offset either way. That holds for the accuracy store and the immersion events if F1.6 moves them to the zone; a pure loader that keeps the UTC default keeps the store's default too.

carries.brief: F9.3 (the declared-domain barrier, card C1): the frequency map's domain changed in F3.2, so declare it from the tree, not from the audit. `FrequencyMap.from_dict` and `FrequencyMap.observe` now share one domain: a decile index in [0, `FREQ_DECILES`), a kW-per-Hz ratio that is finite and in (0, `FREQ_MAX_KW_PER_HZ`], and a count of zero or more. Before F3.2 the update path enforced no upper ratio bound at all (a reading of any kW at 1 Hz folded), so a table row derived from the audit's snapshot would declare the old, unbounded domain.
